cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: AI visibility index shows which brands are disappearing from AI answers
stories.plain: An index tracking brand presence inside AI-generated answers finds that strong Google rankings no longer guarantee visibility in AI responses. Some well-ranked brands barely surface in AI answers at all. This matters because search budgets and SEO strategies built for traditional engines may be leaving brands invisible where buyers increasingly look first.

stories.head: IAB releases updated AI Transparency and Disclosure Framework Version 2 for advertising
stories.plain: The IAB has updated its framework defining when and how advertisers must label AI-generated content in ads, drawing the line around anything that distorts consumer perception of authenticity or identity. Version 2 gives the industry clearer, enforceable guidance — directly shaping how AI-produced creative can legally and ethically run at scale.

stories.head: How to stop overpaying for AI complexity: match the tool to the task
stories.plain: A practical framework explains that rule-based, predictive, generative, and agentic AI carry very different costs and risks, and urges marketers to start with the lightest approach that works. This directly informs buying decisions, helping teams avoid vendor pressure to adopt expensive agentic systems when simpler automation would do the job.

stories.head: Seismic completes merger with Highspot to create unified go-to-market AI platform
stories.plain: Seismic and Highspot have formally merged, combining AI agents, content governance, and sales enablement for 2,500 customers and 3.5 million users. This consolidation reshapes the sales and marketing enablement vendor landscape, reducing buyer choice but potentially raising the bar for integrated AI-driven content and performance tools.

stories.head: Eikona uses reinforcement learning to replace A/B testing with real-time content adaptation
stories.plain: Eikona replaces traditional A/B testing with reinforcement learning that adapts content continuously to individual user behavior. Rather than picking a winner and stopping, the system keeps learning and personalizing. This is a concrete example of bandit-style optimization moving from research into everyday marketing practice.

stories.head: AI visibility index shows which brands are disappearing from AI answers
stories.plain: An index comparing traditional search rankings to AI-answer appearances finds a significant gap: some brands dominate Google but are nearly invisible in AI-generated responses. This matters because generative engine visibility is becoming a separate race from SEO, and marketers who ignore it risk losing discovery to competitors who optimise specifically for AI answers.

stories.head: IAB updates standard for disclosing AI in ads
stories.plain: The IAB's updated AI Transparency and Disclosure Framework v2 sets practical rules for when and how advertisers must label AI-generated or AI-altered ad content, drawing the line at anything that changes perceptions of authenticity or identity. This is the clearest industry-wide AI disclosure standard yet, and it will directly shape how brands govern AI creative going forward.

stories.head: Acoustic launches agentic marketing teammate built on live customer behaviour
stories.plain: Acoustic AI watches real-time customer behaviour, surfaces revenue opportunities and recommends the next campaign move before intent fades. It is a concrete example of agentic decisioning inside a CEP, shifting AI from content helper to autonomous campaign initiator — a step-change in how marketing platforms are being sold and evaluated.

stories.head: How to stop overpaying for AI complexity
stories.plain: A practical framework argues that rule-based, predictive, generative, and agentic AI carry very different cost and risk profiles and that buyers should start with the lightest system that can do the job rather than defaulting to the most sophisticated. This directly shapes how marketing AI should be bought and budgeted, not just hyped.

stories.head: Uniphore launches Marketing AI with digital twins and small language models to move beyond the CDP
stories.plain: Uniphore's new platform uses per-customer digital twins and custom small language models to simulate outcomes before spending and predict next-best actions, positioning itself explicitly as a replacement for traditional CDPs. If it delivers, this signals a structural shift in how customer data infrastructure is built and sold.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Is Erasing Brand Visibility at the Discovery Layer
body: AI-powered search and recommendation engines are quietly rewriting which brands get found — and which vanish. An emerging AI Visibility Index now tracks how brands rank inside LLM outputs, not just on traditional SERPs, revealing that many established names are simply absent from AI-generated answers.

This is a structural shift in product discovery: publishers, social platforms, and AI assistants are all competing to be the new top-of-funnel. Brands that haven't optimised for how AI models cite and surface them are losing ground they may not even know they've lost.

themes.head: The Hidden Debt Inside AI-Accelerated Marketing
body: Speed has a price. As AI tools let teams ship content and campaigns faster, they are also compounding content debt and technical debt at scale — poor-quality, inconsistent, or ungoverned assets that will cost far more to untangle later. Analysts now put the liability of unmanaged content debt at $4.63 trillion globally.

The same dynamic applies inside AI implementations themselves: rushed deployments create model drift, data-quality gaps, and governance holes that quietly accumulate. Leaders who treat AI as a pure productivity lever without auditing downstream debt are essentially borrowing against future agility.

themes.head: Agentic AI Moves from Pilot to Infrastructure
body: Multiple vendors this month shipped multi-agent orchestration layers — coordinated teams of AI agents handling vendor assessments, DataOps pipelines, and real-time customer engagement — signalling that agentic AI is leaving the experimental phase and becoming standard enterprise plumbing. Acoustic, Whistic, Arise, and Uniphore all launched production-grade agentic capabilities in the same window.

The decision that changes is whether to treat AI as a point tool or as a persistent, autonomous teammate embedded in workflows. Organisations that delay agentic architecture decisions now will face integration costs later as these layers harden into de-facto standards.
ev: Agile Brand · Uniphore beyond the CDP

themes.head: AI Disclosure Becomes a Regulatory Baseline
body: The IAB's updated transparency & disclosure framework sets a new industry baseline for labelling AI-generated or AI-assisted advertising creative. This is no longer a voluntary best practice — it is converging toward a compliance expectation that media buyers, publishers, and brands will all be held to.

The strategic implication is immediate: marketing operations teams need disclosure tagging built into creative workflows now, not retrofitted after regulation lands. Brands caught without auditable AI provenance in their ad supply chain will face both reputational and legal exposure.

themes.head: Go-to-Market Consolidation Around AI-Native Revenue Platforms
body: The Seismic–Highspot merger is the clearest signal yet that the sales enablement & GTM intelligence categories are collapsing into fewer, larger, AI-native platforms. Paired with ZoomInfo's reported 600% lift in qualified deals for a client, the message is that data-enriched, AI-orchestrated revenue platforms are pulling decisively ahead of best-of-breed point solutions.

For CMOs and RevOps leaders, this consolidation changes the vendor evaluation frame: the question is no longer which tool covers a specific capability, but which platform owns the full GTM data loop — intent signals, content delivery, and performance analytics — in one governed environment.
ev: MarTech · Next AI opportunity in spend decisions

month.takeaway: Across every theme this month, AI is shifting from optional accelerant to load-bearing infrastructure — meaning the decisions marketers delay today on visibility, debt, agents, disclosure, and platform consolidation will be structurally harder to reverse by 2027.
